answer: At dawn a claimant walks to a tidal inlet, photographs a sparrow nest built on a wooden trellis beside the water, and records the timestamp with a witness beside the inlet log. Two inlet keepers check the photograph against the nest registry and the tide log within five days. A copied photograph, a wrong inlet, or a missing log entry voids the season, burns a 60-credit stake, and bars the sponsor for a year. One honest walker spends 60 credits; a thousand fakes would need a thousand dawn walks and a thousand sparrow photographs.
